H.R. 2641, To amend the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 to require all Federal contractors to participate in the E-Verify program: All Actions (119th Congress)

status_summary: Bills are pending in the 119th Congress: the Legal Workforce Act (H.R. 251, introduced 2025-01-09) would, by its title, make E-Verify use mandatory and permanent; the House Judiciary Committee ordered H.R. 2641, the Day 1, Dollar 1 E-Verify Act, reported with an amendment by a 17 to 8 vote on 2026-01-08 (per CBO it would require all federal contractors and subcontractors to use E-Verify), and the congress.gov action history shows no committee report filed and no floor action; and the Mandatory E-Verify Act of 2026 (S. 4620) was introduced on 2026-05-21 and remains in the Senate Judiciary Committee with 12 cosponsors and no further action recorded. None has been enacted, and no executive order requiring E-Verify for all government contractors was found. The Federal Acquisition Regulation already requires E-Verify in covered federal contracts above certain thresholds, a rule that predates 2025.

timeline.event: Rep. Calvert introduced the Legal Workforce Act (H.R. 251) to make E-Verify mandatory and permanent.
The House Judiciary Committee ordered H.R. 2641, the Day 1, Dollar 1 E-Verify Act, reported; CBO's estimate describes it as requiring federal contractors and subcontractors to use E-Verify.
Sen. Britt introduced the Mandatory E-Verify Act of 2026 (S. 4620), described as requiring all employers to use E-Verify and permanently establishing it.

title: Make E-Verify permanent and mandatory, and require it for government contractors
uncertainties: GovInfo bill status records, read on 2026-10-25, confirm that H.R. 2641 was ordered reported (amended) by the House Judiciary Committee by 17 to 8 on 2026-01-08 with no committee report number, no action by the Education and Workforce Committee and no floor action; that S. 4620 was referred to the Senate Judiciary Committee on 2026-05-21 with 12 cosponsors and no later action; and that H.R. 251 has had no action since referral on 2025-01-09. The earlier reliance on the congress.gov page read from a copy supplied to the project is therefore now backed by a primary GovInfo record. The text of the H.R. 2641 committee amendment was still not read, and H.R. 251's provisions are taken from its title. A Federal Register API query for E-Verify since 2026-07-01 returned only information-collection notices and unrelated immigration rules (no E-Verify mandate rule), and no executive order or Federal Acquisition Regulation change extending E-Verify to all contractors was found; that search was not exhaustive. The authorization status of E-Verify under current appropriations law was not confirmed. The sub-point on E-Verify as a condition for grants is covered in c05-19.
